assertions: Sir William Waller and the Parliamentarian army will overcome Sir Ralph Hopton and the Royalist army in the engagement near Alresford (the Battle of Cheriton) on 29 March 1644
Hopton's side will be defeated and forced to give ground / retreat, failing in the engagement rather than winning or holding it to a draw
Waller's victory will be clear, not marginal: his significators are dignified and strong while Hopton's significator is fallen, peregrine and unaspected
Waller will be well supported in substance and assistants/aid, shown by the Sun, lord of his substance and assistants, in the 10th in the very degree of its exaltation (19° Aries)
Hopton's side will lack ready supplies and support, shown by only Mars and the South Node in the 9th, so no supplies are ready for him
Hopton personally and his cause in this fight are weakened and obscured: Saturn, lord of the 7th, is sub radiis, in his fall, in no aspect to any planet, and square the cusp of the 7th
method: Classical horary astrology (Lilly, Christian Astrology Book II; whole-sign/classical dignities, significator comparison)
reasoning: Queried side taken by Ascendant/Moon with Jupiter and Venus for Waller vs Saturn lord of 7th for Hopton. Waller side: Moon in her exaltation with Jupiter, swift and increasing in light, 11° from Venus; Sun lord of Waller's substance/assistants in 10th at 19° Aries, its exact exaltation degree — honour, strength and effective assistance. Hopton side: Saturn sub radiis, in fall, peregrine, in no aspect to any planet, squaring the 7th cusp — weakness, isolation and affliction; only Mars and South Node in the 9th indicates no supplies ready for him. Strong dignified significators against a fallen unaspected opponent gives a clear victory for the first-named, Waller, per Lilly horary battle rules.
summary: Waller will clearly overcome Hopton at Alresford/Cheriton; the Royalists will be defeated for want of strength, support and ready supplies.
